- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via @objectstack/metadata-protocol)_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via @objectstack/metadata-protocol)_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also reference the affected code. These are **read-only**:

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

> Advisory only. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs origin/main` → pass the list as `args.docs`.

## Docs drift sweep — nothing owed by this change

Swept the whole `content/docs/**` corpus rather than trusting the three-page advisory list,
with this change's own tokens (`seed`, `SeedLoader`, `externalId`, `natural key`,
`reference` near `resolve`, `name` near `lookup|probe|default`, `INVALID_FILTER`,
`dataset`). Release pages excluded — release-owned.

**The live question — does any page document the probe chain, its `name` fallback, or a
seeded boot's log shape? No.** No page anywhere states `externalId → name → id`, or that
reference resolution falls back to `name`, or what a seeded boot's log looks like.

The three advisory pages score **zero** on every token: `concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`
and `protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx` have no hit at all, and
`kernel/services-checklist.mdx` has exactly one — `dataset` in
`/analytics/dataset/query`, a different sense of the word.

Two near-misses checked and both correct as they stand:

- `references/data/seed-loader.mdx` — AUTO-GENERATED — documents
  `ReferenceResolution.targetField` as `optional (default: "name")`. **Still accurate.**
  This change does not touch the metadata-level default: `buildDependencyGraph` still
  stamps `name` on a reference whose target carries no dataset. What became conditional is
  only whether that field is spelled into a database filter. Not hand-edited either way.
- `data-modeling/seed-data.mdx` — describes supplying a lookup's natural key value "(such
  as `name`, `email`, or `code`)" and says the runner resolves it to a database id. True
  before and after; it documents the authoring contract, never the probe order.
- `protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx` — has a "Boot Logs (Example)" block, but it is a
  phase-by-phase startup transcript with no seed or find lines in it.

No pre-existing error found to report either — the pages that touch this area are right,
they simply never described the chain.
